Zelechow New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Żelechów, Poland

Not demolished. Founded around 1802 to replace Żelechów's original cemetery, this site expanded over subsequent decades and served a community that reached 4,016 residents by 1921, most murdered at Treblinka in 1942. During the war, the cemetery held ghetto victims and was also used for German executions; in 1942 it was reportedly the site of a 'black wedding,' a folk ritual believed to ward off typhoid outbreaks. Salomon Epner and Perla Fajgezucht, killed in spring 1945, were among the last people buried there. Poland formally initiated the cemetery's closure by ministerial order in 1964. In 2014, the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage, working with Rabbi Chaim Hopstein and Moses Hirschler, fenced the site and added new matzevot in 2015 honoring tzadikim Aharon ha-Kohen and Arie Hofstein.
